releaseNotes: Platform release: a Formation workspace can now hold people in different jobs. Four roles form an ordinal ladder — viewer, reviewer, editor, owner — and platform/server/domain/capabilities.mjs records one minimum role per capability rather than a role-by-capability grid, so adding a capability is one decision and any role string the ladder does not recognise holds nothing at all. A viewer reads; a reviewer raises questions and records evidence; an editor does the work — workstreams, tasks, decisions, deliverables, drafting, and advancing the launch plan; the owner alone changes what the company is and answers a launch approval. The engine's state, reducer, and catalog are untouched; this manifest advances only to keep root package parity.

Enforcement in the same release: the capability is a required argument to the membership lookup, so a route that does not name what it is doing cannot resolve a member at all. Three surfaces that previously trusted their caller now check for themselves — the execution worker's submit and approval-sync paths and the workspace snapshot builder, which had been handing every decision and all activity history to any member with no role check. The one hand-rolled owner check in execution.mjs is deleted in favour of the shared ladder. A new capabilities test fails on any route in source that is not declared with a capability, then calls all eighteen declared surfaces as a member of each of the four roles and checks the server answered the way the ladder says. Draft requests gain a per-company hourly bound, because inviting someone to do the work also invites them to spend. Checks, 67 domain tests, the production build, and the full audit pass.
